final class CollectionViewController: UIViewController, UICollectionViewDataSource, UICollectionViewDelegate {
    private let handle: String
    private var sort: CollectionSort = .featured
    private var products: [ProductCard] = []
    private var endCursor: String?
    private var hasNextPage = false
    private var isLoading = false
    private var generation = 0
    private var loadTask: Task<Void, Never>?

    private let descriptionLabel = makeLabel(Theme.font(14), Theme.textMuted, lines: 0)
    private var sortChips: [CollectionSort: ChipButton] = [:]
    private var collectionView: UICollectionView!
    private let spinner = makeSpinner()
    private var errorView: MessageStateView?

    private static let selectedSortStyle = ChipButton.Style(height: 32, horizontalPadding: 12, cornerRadius: 16,
                                                            font: Theme.font(13, .semibold), textColor: .white,
                                                            background: Theme.text, borderColor: Theme.text)
    private static let sortStyle = ChipButton.Style(height: 32, horizontalPadding: 12, cornerRadius: 16,
                                                    font: Theme.font(13, .medium), textColor: Theme.text,
                                                    background: Theme.background, borderColor: Theme.border)

    init(handle: String, title: String) {
        self.handle = handle
        super.init(nibName: nil, bundle: nil)
        self.title = title
    }

    required init?(coder: NSCoder) { fatalError() }

    override func viewDidLoad() {
        super.viewDidLoad()
        view.backgroundColor = Theme.background
        installBackButton()

        let descriptionContainer = padded(descriptionLabel, 4, 16, 0, 16)

        let sortRow = HorizontalRow(spacing: 8, height: 32)
        for option in CollectionSort.allCases {
            let chip = ChipButton(title: option.label, style: option == sort ? Self.selectedSortStyle : Self.sortStyle)
            chip.isChosen = option == sort
            chip.accessibilityIdentifier = option.identifier
            chip.onTap = { [weak self] in self?.select(option) }
            sortRow.stack.addArrangedSubview(chip)
            sortChips[option] = chip
        }
        let sortContainer = padded(sortRow, 12, 0, 12, 0)

        collectionView = UICollectionView(frame: .zero, collectionViewLayout: makeLayout())
        collectionView.backgroundColor = Theme.background
        collectionView.accessibilityIdentifier = "product-grid"
        collectionView.dataSource = self
        collectionView.delegate = self
        collectionView.register(ProductGridCell.self, forCellWithReuseIdentifier: ProductGridCell.reuseID)
        collectionView.register(LoadingFooterView.self, forSupplementaryViewOfKind: UICollectionView.elementKindSectionFooter,
                                withReuseIdentifier: LoadingFooterView.reuseID)

        let header = UIStackView(arrangedSubviews: [descriptionContainer, sortContainer])
        header.axis = .vertical
        header.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
        collectionView.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
        view.addSubview(header)
        view.addSubview(collectionView)
        view.addSubview(spinner)
        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
            header.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.safeAreaLayoutGuide.topAnchor),
            header.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.leadingAnchor),
            header.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.trailingAnchor),
            collectionView.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: header.bottomAnchor),
            collectionView.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.leadingAnchor),
            collectionView.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.trailingAnchor),
            collectionView.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.bottomAnchor),
            spinner.centerXAnchor.constraint(equalTo: collectionView.centerXAnchor),
            spinner.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: collectionView.topAnchor, constant: 48),
        ])

        load(reset: true)

content.text:
I fixed the crash. I reproduced it in the simulator using a local replay server that answers in milliseconds, and the same crash no longer happens there. I haven't run it on a physical iPhone.

**Cause.** When the first page of products arrived, the code asked the grid to reload, but UIKit postpones that reload until the next screen update. The "load more near the end" check ran in between and measured the grid while it still looked empty. So it requested page 2 straight away. With a fast server, page 2 arrived before the screen update: the grid still thought it had 0 items while the data reported 48. Inserting 24 items into that mismatch is the invalid update in your crash report. Slow networks always left time for the screen to update between pages, which is why it didn't show up earlier.

**Fix** (in `Everbloom/CollectionViewController.swift`):
- **Data source:** the grid now uses UIKit's diffable data source (`UICollectionViewDiffableDataSource`). UIKit then keeps the grid's item count in step with the data itself, so the mismatch can't happen however fast pages arrive. Each item is identified by its list position plus the current sort order, so changing the sort refreshes the cards.
- **Load-more check:** it now finishes laying out the grid before measuring. It also runs once when the screen appears. Page 2 is no longer fetched until the user actually scrolls near the end; in the replay test, only 12 of 48 collection requests asked for a later page.
- **Search:** it had the same pattern on its list. I applied the same load-more fix there, and it checks the list's row count before inserting.

**Testing.** I added two UI tests that open and scroll several collections, change the sort, and run searches against the replay server on `127.0.0.1:8787`. Before the fix, the collection test crashed in `CollectionViewController.apply(_:)`, both with an empty cache and with a warm one. After the fix it passed twice in a row, the second time with every response served from cache, and the new search test passed both times. The full set of six UI tests passes, and the device release build still compiles with signing disabled.

`NOTES.md` and `BUILD.md` are updated, including how to run the new tests.
